questions.question: The average weight of each box in a consignment of 20 boxes of mangoes and 15 boxes of apples is 30 kg. If the average weight of a box of mangoes is 35 kg, then what is the average weight of a box of apples?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average weight of the mango box = 35,

Number of apple boxes = 15,

Number of mango boxes = 20

**Formula used:**

Weighted average = (w₁× n₁+w₂× n₂)/(n₁+n₂)

Calculation**:**

Let the number of boxes of **mango and apples be n₁ and n₂** 

⇒ n₁ = 20 and n₂ = 15

Let the average weight of **mango box be w₁ and apple box be w₂ **

⇒ w1 = 35 kg and w2 = ?

By using the formula of weighted average and taking value of weighted average as 30 kg,

⇒ 30 = (35×20+15× w₂)/(15+20) 

⇒ 1050 = 700 + 15 × w2 

⇒ w2 = (350)/(15) = (70)/(3)

**The average weight of a box of apples is (70)/(3) kg.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

As per the question, 

The average of Mangoes is increasing by 5 from the common average.

It means that the average of Apple is 5 less than the common average.

So we can say that average weight of the apple box 

⇒ 30(avg) - (5(diff) × 20 (box of mango))/15(box of apples)

⇒30 - (100/15) =70/3

questions.question: The average runs of a cricket player in 20 matches is 30. If the average of the first 12 matches is 40, find the average of the last 8 matches.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total number of matches = 20

Total average runs = 30

**Formula used:**

Average = (sum of observation)/(total number of observation)

Calculation**:**

 By using the formula of average we can calculate the total runs scored by player in 20 matches

⇒ **Total runs = Average runs × Total number of matches**

⇒ Total runs = 30 × 20

⇒ Total runs = 600

Similarly, we can calculate the total runs scored by the player in the first 12 matches,

⇒ R₁₂ = Average runs × Total number of matches

⇒ R12 = 40 × 12 = 480

**The difference between the total runs and total runs in the first 12 matches will give the total runs scored by the player in the last 8 matches**,

⇒ Total runs in last 8 matches = 600 - 480

⇒ Total runs in last 8 matches = 600 - 480 = 120

By using the formula of average,

⇒ Average = (120)/(8)

⇒ Average = 15 runs

**The average of the last 8 matches is 15 runs. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

Average = 30,

Extra runs in first 12 matches = 12 × 10 =120 

This means that the average of the remaining 8 matches will be less by 120 runs, only then the common average will be 30 

⇒ Total runs in last 8 matches = 30 -(120/8) = 30 -15 =15

questions.question: If x-{{1} over x} = 11 and x > 0, what is the value of (x²-{{1} over x²}) ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If x − 1/x = k, then x² − 1/x² = k × √(k² + 4) (for x > 0).

Here, k = 11.

⇒ x² − 1/x² = 11 × √(11² + 4)

⇒ 11 × √(121 + 4) = 11 × 5√5 = 55√5

**∴ The correct answer is 55√5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x − 1/x = 11 and x > 0

**Formula Used:**

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)

(a + b)² = (a − b)² + 4ab

**Calculations:**

⇒ x² − 1/x² = (x − 1/x)(x + 1/x)

First, we find the value of (x + 1/x):

⇒ (x + 1/x)² = (x − 1/x)² + 4

⇒ (x + 1/x)² = 11² + 4 = 121 + 4 = 125

⇒ x + 1/x = √125 = 5√5 (Since x > 0, x + 1/x is positive)

Now, substituting the values into the formula:

⇒ x² − 1/x² = 11 × 5√5 = 55√5

**∴ The correct answer is 55√5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum and Difference Relation

If x + 1/x = k, then x − 1/x = ±√(k² − 4).

Sum of Squares Relation

If x − 1/x = k, then x² + 1/x² = k² + 2.

Sum of Cubes Relation

If x − 1/x = k, then x³ − 1/x³ = k³ + 3k.

questions.question: The ratio of the cost price to the marked price of an article is 4 ∶ 7. A discount of 25% is given on the marked price and the shopkeeper made a profit of ₹50. Find the cost price of the article.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Cost price : Marked price = 4 : 7

Discount = 25%

Profit = Rs 50

**Formula used**

(C)/(M)=(100-D)/(100+P)

C = cost price

M = marked price

D = discount%

P = profit%

**Calculation**

(C)/(M)=(100-D)/(100+P)=(100-25)/(100+P)=(4)/(7)

from this P = 31.25%

31.25% of C = 50Rs

then, C is 100% which is (50)/(31.25)times 100=160Rs

**The cost price of the article is **Rs **160**

questions.question: A shopkeeper claims that he is selling rice at Rs.27/kg which cost him Rs.30/kg, but he gives 750 grams instead of 1000 grams. What is his profit or loss percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net multiplier (SP/CP) = (Claimed SP ÷ Actual CP) × (True Weight ÷ Faulty Weight)

Ratio = (27 ÷ 30) × (1000 ÷ 750) = (9/10) × (4/3)

Net Ratio = 36 ÷ 30 = 6 ÷ 5

Profit % = (6 − 5) ÷ 5 × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Cost Price (CP)** of 1000 g rice = ₹30

**Selling Price (SP)** of 750 g rice (claimed as 1000 g) = ₹27

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b03f37dac48feea435079d448a0f0961354595e943d7c29ce686eec4a080f6f1.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Actual **Cost Price** of 1000 g rice = ₹30

⇒ Actual **Cost Price** of 750 g rice = (30 ÷ 1000) × 750

⇒ Actual **Cost Price** of 750 g rice = ₹22.5

⇒ Given **Selling Price** of 750 g rice = ₹27

⇒ **Total Profit** = SP − CP = 27 − 22.5 = ₹4.5

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (4.5 ÷ 22.5) × 100

⇒ **Profit Percentage** = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer sells at a profit/loss on price and also uses a **faulty weight**, the net gain/loss is calculated by the product of individual multiplication factors.

Profit with Weight Manipulation

Profit % = [(True Value − False Value) ÷ False Value] × 100. In this problem, the dealer also changed the price, so we compare the **actual CP of the weight delivered** with the **actual SP received**.

Successive Percentage Change

Net Profit % can be viewed as successive changes: price reduction (10% loss) and weight manipulation (33.33% profit). Net = −10 + 33.33 + (−10 × 33.33)/100 = 20%.
